subject: English
questionText:
Choose the correct active voice transformation of the sentence:

The renowned author's newest novel will have been released by the end of the year.

options.A: The renowned author will have been releasing his newest novel by the end of the year.
options.B: The renowned author will release his newest novel by the end of the year.
options.C: The renowned author will have released his newest novel by the end of the year.
options.D: The renowned author has released his newest novel by the end of the year.

solution:
Rule: Future Perfect Passive → Future Perfect Active.
The given sentence is in the future perfect passive tense: "will have been released". To convert it into active voice, the agent "the renowned author" becomes the subject, and "will have been released" changes to "will have released".
Therefore, the correct active voice sentence is: "The renowned author will have released his newest novel by the end of the year."
Correct Answer: (3)

questionText:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The chef had prepared the special dish. [SSC CHSL Tier 1, 14 Nov 2025, Shift-2]

options.A: The special dish was prepared by the chef.
options.B: The special dish had been prepared by the chef.
options.C: The special dish has been prepared by the chef.
options.D: The special dish is being prepared by the chef.

solution:
Rule: The past perfect active voice ('had prepared') converts to the past perfect passive voice ('had been prepared').
The active sentence "The chef had prepared the special dish" is in the past perfect tense. To convert to passive, the object 'the special dish' becomes the subject. The verb phrase 'had prepared' changes to 'had been prepared'.
Option 1 uses the simple past. Option 3 uses the present perfect. Option 4 uses the present continuous.
Correct Answer is The special dish had been prepared by the chef because it correctly uses the past perfect passive.
Ans: The special dish had been prepared by the chef.

questionText: Change the following sentence into the Active form: The report is expected to be delivered by the committee next week. [SSC CHSL Tier 1, 15 Nov 2025, Shift-1]

options.A: The committee is expecting to deliver the report next week.
options.B: The committee is expected to deliver the report next week.
options.C: The committee expects to deliver the report next week.
options.D: The committee will deliver the report next week.

solution:
Rule: When converting from passive to active, identify the subject performing the action. The passive structure 'is expected to be delivered' becomes active 'is expected to deliver'.
The passive sentence "The report is expected to be delivered by the committee..." has 'the committee' as the doer. To make it active, 'the committee' becomes the subject. The verb phrase becomes 'is expected to deliver'.
Option 1 is a passive construction. Option 3 changes the meaning. Option 4 changes the meaning.
Correct Answer is The committee is expected to deliver the report next week because it correctly identifies the subject and uses the active infinitive.
Ans: The committee is expected to deliver the report next week.

questionText: Change the following sentence into the Active form: It was believed that the secret formula had been stolen by a rival company. [SSC CHSL Tier 1, 15 Nov 2025, Shift-2]

options.A: A rival company believed that the secret formula had been stolen.
options.B: People believed that a rival company had stolen the secret formula.
options.C: The secret formula was stolen by a rival company.
options.D: A rival company stole the secret formula, it was believed.

solution:
Rule: When converting from passive to active, identify the logical subject performing the action. The passive structure 'It was believed that... had been stolen' becomes active 'People believed that... had stolen...'.
The passive sentence "It was believed that the secret formula had been stolen by a rival company" has 'a rival company' as the doer. To make it active, a logical subject like 'People' is introduced. The verb phrase becomes 'People believed that a rival company had stolen'.
Option 1 is a passive construction. Option 3 is a passive construction. Option 4 is awkward and changes the structure.
Correct Answer is People believed that a rival company had stolen the secret formula because it correctly introduces a logical subject and uses the active past perfect.
Ans: People believed that a rival company had stolen the secret formula.

questionText:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Will the sponsors invite the whole team to the party?

options.A: Will the whole team invite to the party by the sponsors?
options.B: Will the whole team invite the sponsors to the party?
options.C: Will the whole team been invited to the party by the sponsors?
options.D: Will the whole team be invited to the party by the sponsors?

solution:
Rule: For a question in the simple future tense, the passive voice is formed using 'Will + subject + be + past participle?'.
The active question "Will the sponsors invite...?" is in the simple future tense. To convert to passive, the object 'the whole team' becomes the subject. The verb phrase 'will invite' becomes 'will be invited'.
Option 1 is missing 'be'. Option 2 is active. Option 3 is grammatically incorrect.
Correct Answer is Will the whole team be invited to the party by the sponsors? because it correctly uses the future simple passive interrogative.
Ans: Will the whole team be invited to the party by the sponsors?
